text:
maya.ops: FYI - scheduling a preflight pager simulation during next maintenance window. want to validate alert routing + rollback play before we touch production caching layer. ETA Tue 23:00 UTC (window 23:00-23:30).

jon.sre: +1. what's the exact scope? full kv-cache drain or canary only?

maya.ops: canary only on-controlplane -> drain 10% of serving nodes in eu-west1 then observe for 10m. no schema or customer-facing DB changes.

samira.support: we'll prepare a customer-facing note just in case. prefer to send only if impact occurs.

incident-bot: Scheduled maintenance created: maintenance/2490012345. Pager test will fire simulated Paging:SERVING-ERROR for canary if synthetic check fails.

maya.ops: test flow:
- 23:00 start canary drain (10% of serving pool, eu-west1)
- 23:02 run synthetic load + success/error checks (automated)
- 23:12 evaluate metrics (error rate, tail latency, 5xx spikes)
- 23:15 either continue rollout to 50% or execute rollback if thresholds hit

jon.sre: Rollback criteria (agreed):
- error rate > 2% sustained for 3 minutes OR
- 95th percentile token latency increase > 1s vs baseline OR
- CPU/GPU OOM or runaway memory growth on any canary node

jon.sre: Rollback command is `./scripts/rollback-serving.sh --maintenance-id 2490012345` (ops-only). runbook link: #eng-runbooks-serving (see rollback checklist).

maya.ops: paging rules for the sim: we want to validate that on-call receives the page and that the bridge auto-opens. do NOT escalate to execs for the sim. use @oncall-rotation for primary.

oncall-rotation: i'll be primary for the sim. will ack and run playbook if page fires. please DM me if you want to join bridge.

maya.ops: Customer comms drafts below — only send if customer-visible impact (>= 1% of requests impacted for > 5 min). keep short.

--- statuspage draft ---
We are conducting a scheduled maintenance activity to validate our serving node rollout process. Some customers may experience brief intermittent increases in latency while we test a canary. We will post updates here if any customer impact is detected. Scheduled: Tue 23:00 UTC, duration ~30 minutes.
--- end ---

--- support email/SMS template ---
Subject: Brief maintenance test may affect LLM response latency
Body: Hi — Scheduled maintenance/test underway starting Tue 23:00 UTC. You may see brief latency increases (<5 min) for a subset of requests. If you see errors or degraded service, reply to this message and our support team will escalate.
--- end ---

samira.support: i'll queue the template in Intercom and mark it 'send-on-impact'. also prepping a short triage checklist for Tier 1.

maya.ops: monitoring alerts to watch (synthetic and prod):
- Serving synthetic check: synthetic-llm-eu-west1 (should stay green)
- 5xx spike alert: serving-5xx-rate-eu-west1
- Latency tail: serving-latency-p95-token-eu-west1
- Memory OOM: serving-node-memory-critical

jon.sre: If page happens:
1) ack and join the bridge (incident-bot will post bridge URL)
2) run quick triage: check logs, recent deploys, node resource graphs, KV cache hit ratios
3) if thresholds met, run rollback script (see above) and post command output in channel
4) post status to statuspage and support channel: short bullet points

maya.ops: bridge policy for the sim: only oncall + core SREs. others watch-only. please do not DM-explore unless asked.

lia-ux: small ask — if we actually hit customer-visible impact and we publish to StatusPage, could the message include our timeline for followups? (so customers know when postmortem will be available)

maya.ops: yes — we'll add: "We will post a follow-up with details and root cause within 24 hours if there is customer impact."

incident-bot: Pager simulation will trigger at 23:05 if synthetic fails. Reminder: this is a test; do not escalate beyond SRE leads.

jon.sre: quick checklist snippet to paste in bridge once page fires:
```
- ack page
- check synthetic dashboard (last 15m)
- grep recent errors in logs: `kubectl logs -l app=serving --since=15m | grep \"ERROR\"`
- check KV cache hit ratio
- decide: continue -> expand canary or rollback -> run rollback-serving.sh
```

maya.ops: post-maint actions (if sim is clean):
- announce completion here + small note on StatusPage that maintenance completed with no impact
- run a followup synthetic for 1h to ensure no regressions
- doc update: add any lessons to ops-maint-runbook.md

samira.support: if we do rollback and customers were impacted, i'll send the prepared email within 15m and escalate to account reps.

jon.sre: one last thing — if the rollback script fails, escalate to oncall pager with tag P0 and call SRE lead (maya.ops) directly. include `--force` only after approval.

maya.ops: thanks everyone. quick ask: if you plan to watch the bridge actively, react with :eyes: so i can limit invites.

jon.sre: :eyes:

samira.support: :eyes:

oncall-rotation: :eyes: i'll be on bridge 22:50 UTC to pre-check dashboards.

incident-bot: Maintenance window reminder scheduled for Tue 22:45 UTC.

maya.ops: closing note: this sim is meant to validate humans + tooling. assume we will abort early on any sign of customer risk. see you all Tuesday. :rocket:

maya.ops (23:20 UTC): Canary passed 10m checks, expanding to 50% held for 5m - no action needed.

jon.sre (23:27 UTC): 50% held for 5m, all green. rolling back to normal traffic routing, finishing maintenance early.

incident-bot (23:30 UTC): Maintenance 2490012345 marked complete.

maya.ops (23:32 UTC): Completed — no customer impact. posting statuspage completion note and closing thread.

--- statuspage completion ---
Scheduled maintenance completed successfully. No customer impact detected. We will continue to monitor and will publish any follow-up if needed.
--- end ---
